__comment: NVisionX Scan Activity Overview — CENTRAL (all clusters) variant of scan-activity-overview.json. mimir's central Grafana has no direct network path into any environment's VPC (no peering/Transit Gateway exists to any of them), so panels needing live per-document OpenSearch queries or CloudWatch AWS/ES metrics can't reach those sources directly from here - unlike Prometheus, which already arrives via remote_write (push, not pull) from each environment. Files/bytes totals, by-connector and by-datasource breakdowns, and their time trends are now sourced from nx_scan_files_total / nx_scan_bytes_total / nx_scan_files_by_datasource - Prometheus gauges published by a small per-environment exporter (nx-scan-metrics-exporter, see that repo's README) that queries OpenSearch locally and rides the same existing remote_write path everything else uses. Gauges are re-read from OpenSearch every scrape, so a pod restart never causes a visible dip; the by-connector/by-datasource time-series panels use delta() over the panel interval to approximate 'new files in this window' from the running totals. Two panel groups were REMOVED rather than left broken: 'Recent scanned files' (needs live per-document OpenSearch queries, no Prometheus equivalent) and the AWS/ES CloudWatch domain-health row (needs a CloudWatch datasource, not yet registered anywhere centrally). Their opensearch_ds/cloudwatch_ds template variables had zero matching datasources on this Grafana, which made the WHOLE dashboard fail to import via the sync tool (not just those panels going blank) - removing them was required to get anything to show up at all. Re-add both once real OpenSearch + CloudWatch datasources exist centrally.
title: NVisionX — Scan Activity Overview (All Clusters)

panels.title: Files scanned (records)
panels.description: Current total document count in OpenSearch (*-nxidx-*), summed across connectors. Sourced from nx_scan_files_total (nx-scan-metrics-exporter), a gauge re-read from OpenSearch every scrape — not scoped to the time picker like the old per-document query was, since this is a running total, not new-in-range.

panels.title: Total size of scanned files
panels.description: Current total 'size' (bytes) of scanned files across connectors. Sourced from nx_scan_bytes_total (nx-scan-metrics-exporter) — a running total, not scoped to the time picker.

panels.title: Scans running NOW
panels.description: In-flight messages across all *-scanner-v1 NATS consumers. Live gauge — independent of the time range.

panels.title: Backlog (pending)
panels.description: Files queued but not yet picked up by scanners. Live gauge.

panels.title: Files scanned over time (by connector)
panels.description: New files per interval, approximated as delta() of the running nx_scan_files_total gauge (not a per-bucket count query like the old OpenSearch date_histogram).

panels.title: Data scanned over time
panels.description: New bytes per interval, approximated as delta() of the running nx_scan_bytes_total gauge.

panels.title: Scan health (running fine vs failing). NOTE: authoritative per-scan-run success/failed lives in the Postgres app DB; this row is a live NATS-redelivery proxy until a Postgres datasource is added.
Redeliveries / retries by source (processing-error proxy)
panels.description: nats_consumer_num_redelivered rising = messages failing and being retried. Sustained growth indicates a scan is NOT running fine. Authoritative per-scan status requires the Postgres scan-jobs table (follow-up).

panels.title: Recent scanned files and OpenSearch domain health are not available centrally yet — both need direct connectivity/datasources this Grafana doesn't have (see file header comment). Removed from this dashboard rather than shown broken; will return once OpenSearch/CloudWatch datasources exist centrally.
